sentences.text:
"It is therefore humbly prayed that the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash the FIR registered in connection with Crime No. 916 of 2022 at PS Kota, District Bilaspur, CG registered against the present petitioners for offence under Section 420,
467, 468, 471, 120B read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code in view of compromise/ settlement arrived between the parties.

Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deem fit and proper may also kindly be granted to the petitioners in the interest of justice."
3) Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and respondent No.2 would submit that dispute between the parties has already been settled.

They further submit that the statement of the parties regarding the settlement of dispute has been recorded before the learned Additional Registrar (Judicial) of this Court on 12.09.2023, where they categorically stated that they have settled the dispute and arrived at a settlement without any coercion, greed, or pressure.
4) From documents, it appears that an FIR was registered against the petitioners for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B read with 34 of the IPC.

5) Vide order dated 12.09.2023, petitioners and respondent No.2 were directed to appear before the Additional Registrar (Judicial) of the Registry of this Court on the same day i.e. on 12.09.2023 for recording their statements.

In pursuance of the above order, the petitioners as well as respondent No.2 appeared before the Registrar (Judicial)/ Additional Registrar (Judicial) on 12.09.2023 and their statements were recorded, where they have expressed their desire to enter into compromise without any coercion, greed, or pressure.
6)
Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 would submit that statement of respondent No.2 has already been recorded before the Additional Registrar (Judicial) on 12.09.2023.

He would further submit that as parties have settled their dispute, therefore, respondent No.2 does not want to pursue this criminal case furthermore against all the petitioners and thus, the order for quashment of FIR in Crime No.916/2022 may be passed.
7) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents.

8) The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in the matter of 'Ramgopal And Another Vs State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 834' and 'Narinder Singh and Others Vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2014(6) SCC 466', that the matters which can be categorized as personal in nature or in the matter in which the nature of injuries do not exhibit mental depravity or commission of an offence of such a serious nature that quashing of which would override public interest, the Court can quash the FIR in view of the settlement arrived at amongst the parties.
